citations.assessment: The checked Semachot has the visit to ben Zakkai in Babylonia and channels of wine and oil.
Tosefta has Kavul and the channels of wine and oil, without naming ben Zakkai or Tarfon.
The sons of Rabban Gamliel bathe in Kavul and face local objection.
The Bavli also narrates the Biri footwear objection. The checked line does not specify gold.
The Tosefta preserves both local objections and gives the golden footwear detail in brackets.
The Mishnah gives the maxim to Hillel, without identifying him by patronymic.
The explicit cross-reference distinguishes this Hillel from Hillel the Elder and names Yehudah Nesia as his brother.

notes.text: The alternate Semachot host and location require a directly identified edition. The checked Semachot has ben Zakkai and Babylonia, while the checked Tosefta mentions Kavul without a host. Searches for the stated Tarfon phrase did not establish its source.
The witnesses do not settle which Gamliel is meant. Semachot and both Tosefta accounts lack the required patronymic. Zacuto’s own argument favors Yavneh, while Heilprin leaves alternatives.

The exact Chikkur Din and Yad Yehudah witnesses remain open. Connector lookup and targeted transcription discovery did not produce the two passages; Heilprin’s parallel in entry 3421 confirms the cross-reference only.

The identification of this Mishnah’s Hillel as Yehudah’s brother remains a reading. The Mishnah gives only Hillel. Heilprin 3421 states the identification and explicitly reports competing interpretation.
